slides.title: Vision & Focus
slides.brief: Subtitle: Four strategic pillars guide our 2026 investment decisions, anchored by breakout platform momentum. Pillars (icon / title / description): 1) smart_toy / Agent Platform / Ship the industry's most reliable autonomous agent runtime for enterprise workloads. 2) hub / Open Ecosystem / Double the partner marketplace to 400+ integrations across every major SaaS platform. 3) security / Trust by Design / Extend zero-trust architecture with SOC 2 Type II, FedRAMP, and EU AI Act readiness. 4) public / Global Scale / Operate 14 regions at 99.99% uptime while entering Japan and Brazil markets. Metrics (value / label): 168% / ARR Growth YoY; 312 / Enterprise Customers; 71 / Enterprise NPS; 99.98% / Platform Uptime.

slides.title: Market Position
slides.brief: Subtitle: Enterprise AI spend is consolidating around agentic platforms — and our segment is growing fastest. Left zone label: Key Growth Drivers. Drivers (number / title / description): 01 / Agentic Shift / Buyers now prioritize autonomous execution over chat interfaces, tripling agent tooling budgets. 02 / Platform Consolidation / Enterprises want one governed platform instead of 12 point tools; RFP counts dropped 40%. 03 / Developer Gravity / 12,000 active builders on the Atlas SDK create switching costs and marketplace pull. 04 / Compliance Pressure / EU AI Act and sector rules make auditable, in-VPC deployment a purchase requirement. Right chart card: icon pie_chart, title 'Enterprise AI Spend by Segment', subtitle 'Share of 2026 market', canvas id 'marketChart', data [34, 28, 22, 16] with labels Agent Platforms, Copilots & Assistants, Model APIs, Legacy Automation. Center text: $56B / 2026 Market. Legend rows in order: Agent Platforms 34%, Copilots & Assistants 28%, Model APIs 22%, Legacy Automation 16%. Chart follows references/chart-recipes.md exactly.

slides.title: Target Personas
slides.brief: Subtitle: Winning the platform decision starts with the VP of Engineering — the budget owner who feels integration pain most. Left zone label: Top Pain Points. Pains (icon / title / description): extension / Tool Sprawl / 17 average SaaS tools per team with no shared context between them. integration_instructions / Integration Debt / Six-month backlogs for custom connectors block every new rollout. policy / Governance Gaps / Shadow AI deployments grow with no audit trail for regulators. engineering / Talent Scarcity / Platform engineers are impossible to hire; teams wait months to build. Center persona card: avatar icon person, name Sarah Chen, role VP Engineering, Global 2000. Quote: "I don't need another copilot. I need one platform my teams can build on — and that our auditors can trust." Stats: 2,400 / Engineers in Org and $18M / Annual AI Budget. Right zone label: Decision Chain. Steps (1-4, title / description): 1 Problem Framing / Platform-versus-point-tools mandate set by the engineering leadership team. 2 Technical Eval / Four-week proof of concept with two product teams on real workloads. 3 Security Review / SOC 2, VPC deployment, customer-managed keys, and audit-log checks. 4 Exec Sign-off / CFO-led ROI case with an 18-month payback commitment.

slides.brief: DARK page: .ppt-slide bg-[#0A2540]; white title; subtitle: Three commitments define success for 2026 — each with a hard number attached. Title-block right chip: FY2026 Targets. slides.title: Budget & Risk
slides.brief: Subtitle: A $30M plan weighted toward R&D, with the four risks we are actively managing. Left chart card: icon account_balance_wallet, title 'Budget Allocation', subtitle 'FY2026 distribution', canvas id 'budgetChart', data [45, 30, 15, 10] with labels R&D, GTM, Infrastructure, G&A. Center text: $30M / Total Budget. Legend rows (amounts): R&D $13.5M; GTM $9.0M; Infrastructure $4.5M; G&A $3.0M. Chart follows references/chart-recipes.md (h-[240px] canvas on this archetype). Right zone label: Key Risks & Mitigation. Risks (title / description / mitigation / severity): Runtime Reliability / Scaling from 4K to 50K daily workloads risks p95 latency breaches and cascading failures. / Chaos testing, per-tenant isolation, and a 400ms SLO with automated rollback. / HIGH. Pricing Pressure / Hyperscaler bundles could compress per-seat pricing by 20-30% in renewal cycles. / Shift revenue mix toward usage-based workloads and marketplace take-rate. / HIGH. Regulatory Timing / EU AI Act control deadlines may land before our Q3 GA date. / Dedicated compliance squad with external counsel review at every milestone. / MEDIUM. Talent Concentration / Deep runtime knowledge sits with six engineers; attrition is a single point of failure. / Pair-rotation program, documentation sprints, and two senior backfills in Q1. / MEDIUM.
